info.name: sandbox-runner
info.description:
sandbox-runner endpoints, called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/sandbox` → `http://sandbox-runner:8000`, `include_subpath: true`). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth. See ai/sandbox/ENDPOINTS.md for the full endpoint reference and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

Sessions: the workflow is get_runtime_types → create → write_files (loop with get_files / get_logs / exec) → preview → close. Or the one-shot: run. First call: omit `session_id`; server generates one and returns it. Follow-up call: pass the same `session_id` back — server writes new files into the running container's /app, returns the same URL, dev server hot-reloads. Set the `sandboxSessionId` collection variable from the first response, then run the follow-up request. See ai/sandbox/SANDBOX.md § MCP tool flow.

File tools follow Claude Code's contract: write_files for NEW files, read_file (GET /session/{id}/file) for a numbered window, edit_file (POST /session/{id}/edit) for exact-string changes.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `sandbox-runner.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents its request body, its success response and every error status whose body is more than FastAPI's `{"detail": "<message>"}`. Any other error answers that `{"detail": "<message>"}`; a request that fails FastAPI's own validation answers 422 `{"detail": [{"type", "loc", "msg", "input", ...}]}`, one entry per problem. A request sent through LiteLLM (`{{litellm}}`) can also be refused by LiteLLM itself before it reaches the service -- 401 / 403 for a missing or unauthorised key -- with LiteLLM's `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}`.

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). The pass-through runs with `auth: true`, so a non-admin virtual key needs `/v1/sandbox` in its (or its team's) `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes` — set under `metadata`, by a proxy admin, because the top-level field is Enterprise-only; the master key works without it. Otherwise 403. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth.

12-char hex id returned by POST /run as `sandbox_id`. Fill in after spawning to run the /jobs/{id} + DELETE /jobs/{id} requests. This changes on every spawn — for a stable handle across turns use `sandboxSessionId`.

Persistent session handle returned by POST /run as `session_id`. Paste it here and it's used by the 'update in-session' + 'delete files' + 'DELETE /session' requests below. Passing the same value back to POST /run updates the running container's files in place — same URL, dev server hot-reloads.

MCP transport session id — paste in the `mcp-session-id` response header value returned by the `MCP — initialize` request. Subsequent MCP calls need it. UNRELATED to `sandboxSessionId` — this one is FastMCP's HTTP-transport session cookie, not the sandbox reuse handle.

Optional chat/conversation id (^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,128}$) for the one-sandbox-per-chat guard. Passed as `chat_id` on POST /create and POST /run (and the create/run MCP tools). When set, a second create for the same chat returns the existing session (`duplicate_create_prevented: true`) instead of spawning a duplicate, and a run with no session_id reuses the chat's running container. Leave empty to keep always-spawn behavior. Distinct from `sandboxSessionId` (the per-preview handle) and `mcpSessionId` (the FastMCP transport cookie).

body.raw:
{
  "runtime": "python",
  "files": {
    "app.py": "import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

st.title('sine wave demo')
n = st.slider('samples', 10, 500, 100)
freq = st.slider('frequency', 1, 10, 3)
x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n)
df = pd.DataFrame({'x': x, 'y': np.sin(freq * x)})
st.line_chart(df.set_index('x'))
"
  },
  "ttl_seconds": 900
}

request.description:
Spawn a Streamlit sandbox. Runtime `python` base image has streamlit, gradio, flask, fastapi, pandas, numpy, matplotlib, plotly, requests, pillow pre-installed. Add a requirements.txt to files to install additional deps via sandbox-egress (pypi allowlisted). Cold-start ~2s pre-baked; 20-90s if pip install runs.

#### Schemas

See *POST /run — static HTML*, the first request of this endpoint.

Illustrates the install-if-present pattern. If files contains a requirements.txt, the base image entrypoint runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` before executing the command. pip goes through HTTP_PROXY=sandbox-egress:8888 and hits the pypi.org / files.pythonhosted.org allowlist.

#### Schemas

See *POST /run — static HTML*, the first request of this endpoint.

Spawn a Node sandbox. Base image has serve, vite, react, react-dom, express, next installed globally so `require('express')` works without a package.json. Add a package.json to files to trigger `npm install` on boot.

#### Schemas

See *POST /run — static HTML*, the first request of this endpoint.

Multi-file Vite + React counter. Vite HMR uses WebSockets — sandbox-proxy (Caddy) forwards them by default, so buttons work end-to-end when iframed.

#### Schemas

See *POST /run — static HTML*, the first request of this endpoint.

Update a preview in place. Pass the `session_id` from a previous /run response (via the sandboxSessionId collection variable) and the file(s) that changed. The runner writes them into the running container's /app via docker cp — no respawn. Response has `reused: true` and the SAME sandbox_id + url as the initial spawn. The dev server inside the sandbox reloads on file change: nginx serves the new file on next request, Streamlit auto-reruns, Vite HMR fires without a browser refresh. If the container was already reaped when this call arrives (idle-TTL or manual rm), the runner self-heals — same session_id, new sandbox_id, new url — so callers don't have to distinguish the two cases.

`files` is treated as an overlay: paths listed here overwrite the running container's copies; unlisted files stay put. Save tokens by not resending unchanged files.

Rewrite guard: on this follow-up path a listed file that already exists as a text file of 30+ lines and keeps >= 50% of its lines is refused with 409 rewrite_of_existing_file unless `overwrite` is true (same rule as POST /session/{id}/files). Change part of a file with POST /session/{id}/edit instead.

#### Schemas

See *POST /run — static HTML*, the first request of this endpoint.

Explicitly remove file(s) from a running sandbox. Use on follow-up calls when the model renames or drops a file — otherwise stale files linger, because overlay semantics on `files` never delete. Paths are relative to /app; absolute paths and '..' return 400. Combine with a `files` map to atomically add + remove in one call.

Ignored on the first call (no session_id) — the container starts fresh from `files` alone, there's nothing to delete.

#### Schemas

See *POST /run — static HTML*, the first request of this endpoint.

request.description:
Read files back from /app, raw. Binary payloads come back base64-encoded — same shape you can round-trip via POST /session/{id}/files. A truncated text file is cut on a UTF-8 character boundary. Missing paths get an `error: 'not found'` entry and a directory path an `error: '<path> is a directory.'` entry rather than raising. For source a model is about to change, GET /session/{id}/file (numbered line windows) is the better read. See ENDPOINTS.md § GET /session/{session_id}/files.

#### Schemas

request.description:
Explicitly tear down the running sandbox for a session. Backs sandbox.close. Idempotent — returns 204 whether or not the session existed. Distinct from DELETE /jobs/{sandbox_id}: /jobs targets a specific spawn event by its 12-char internal id, while /session targets whatever's currently running under the persistent session handle (may have been respawned via self-heal since the model last saw it).

Errors: 400 if session_id fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, 500 if the runner isn't initialized.

#### Schemas

Idempotent: an unknown or expired session is a 204 too. 400 an invalid `session_id`.

Response `204`: no body — no body.

variable.description: Persistent session handle returned by POST /run as session_id.

request.description:
Stream the running sandbox's /app back as a tar archive (Content-Type: application/x-tar, Content-Disposition: attachment). Docker daemon does the packing (container.get_archive) so nothing buffers in the runner. Session-based, so this URL keeps working across self-heal spawns — resolves session_id → current container at request time.

Also exposed publicly via the sandbox-proxy Caddy route at ${SANDBOX_PROXY_URL}/download/{sandboxSessionId} (e.g. https://chat.zeoenergy.com/sandboxes/download/…) so browsers can download the archive with the same oauth2-proxy auth as the preview iframe. run / preview response text includes this URL on the 'Download source:' line — models share it verbatim when a user asks to save the code.

Errors: 400 if session_id fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, 404 if there's no running sandbox for this session (never existed, or reaped without self-heal).

Postman note: click 'Send and Download' to save the response as a file. The tar root is `app/`, so `tar -xf sandbox-*.tar` extracts to `./app/`.

#### Schemas

Follows self-heal: the session's CURRENT sandbox. 400 an invalid `session_id`, 404 no running sandbox (or its container is gone).

Response `200` (`application/x-tar`) — The container's /app as a plain tar stream (archive root `app/`), `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="sandbox-<sandbox_id>.tar"`.

query.description: Trailing lines to return. Default 100, clamped 1..1000.

variable.description: Persistent session handle returned by POST /run as session_id.

request.description:
Direct download by internal sandbox_id — bypasses session resolution. Useful for operators who want to grab the archive from a SPECIFIC spawn event even if the session self-healed to a different container since. Same tar shape as the session variant. Prefer /session/{id}/download for end-user download links because that URL keeps working across self-heal.

Errors: 404 if no sandbox with that id, 409 if the sandbox exists in the registry but never reached the `running` phase (no container to export).

#### Schemas

404 no such sandbox (or its container is gone), 409 it never reached `running`.

Response `200` (`application/x-tar`) — The container's /app as a plain tar stream (archive root `app/`), `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="sandbox-<sandbox_id>.tar"`.

request.description:
Tear a sandbox down early. Stops the container, removes it, deletes the row, releases the concurrency slot. Returns 204 no body. 404 if the sandbox id is unknown.

#### Schemas

Stops the container, deletes the row, releases the slot if it held one. 404 no such sandbox.

Response `204`: no body — no body.

variable.description: 12-char hex id of the target sandbox (NOT session_id). The shim inside the browser reads this from the URL path prefix; operators calling this directly need the id from POST /run's `sandbox_id` field.

item.name: MCP
item.description:
FastMCP JSON-RPC over HTTP forwarded through the LiteLLM pass-through. Note that LiteLLM ALSO advertises the sandbox as an MCP server via `mcp_servers.sandbox` in litellm_config.yaml — models see the tool through that path, not this one. The Postman requests below are useful for debugging the transport directly. Every MCP request MUST use trailing-slash (POST /mcp/), MUST send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, and MUST start with an `initialize` call — copy the `mcp-session-id` response header into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable for subsequent calls.

Tools registered on the sandbox MCP server: get_runtime_types, create, write_files, read_file, edit_file, get_files, get_logs, exec, preview, close, list_sessions, run. The examples below cover the primary tools.
